clue.text: Clapped out in the next valley?

definitions.meaning: worn out and past one's best, as an old person or machine might be
taken literally, somewhere on the far side of the rise that separates two valleys

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being past one's prime also literally describes a place beyond the ridge.

clue.text: Rearranged live coverage

indicators.note: the letters of the word live are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone reorganises the live broadcast schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage' suggests news reporting, but here it means a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin piece of fabric worn over the face is a form of covering.

clue.text: Francis dropped many a tool

indicators.note: the letter standing for many is let fall from the surname

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan sailor
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Francis let fall many a tool from his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the English Elizabethan navigator; lose D (500 in Roman numerals, so 'many') and you are left with the garden implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled toothed implement for gathering leaves is a garden tool.

clue.text: Promising applicant

definitions.meaning: a candidate seeking a job or a place

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning likely to succeed and a noun for someone aspiring to a post.

clue.text: Timothy denied entering town near Manchester

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words Timothy denied, going into them

explanation.surface: Timothy says he never went into a town near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'Timothy denied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde is a market town in Greater Manchester, a few miles east of the city.

clue.text: Host Leo coming from the country

indicators.note: the letters of Host Leo are worked into something new that emerges from them

explanation.surface: A host named Leo arrives from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Hard work at joint using oily matter

parts.note: the elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm
grease is thick oily lubricant

explanation.surface: A mechanic does hard graft on a joint with lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow grease is an idiom for vigorous physical effort, such as polishing.

clue.text: Anticipating including alternative drug

indicators.note: the word for anticipating takes the word for alternative inside it

parts.note: expectant means waiting for something to happen
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone awaits a different medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectorant is a medicine that helps bring up phlegm from the chest.

clue.text: Following law, it can be bent but should not be broken

definitions.text: it can be bent but should not be broken

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A rule, like the law, may be bent but never broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rule being bent; the definition is the flexible electrical cable, which bends but must not break.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric cable on an appliance bends easily but becomes dangerous if its wires snap.

clue.text: Create disturbance that could cloud one's view

definitions.meaning: to make a fuss or cause trouble
taken literally, stirring up dirt from the ground obscures sight

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for causing a commotion also literally means raising dirt into the air.

clue.text: Engineer's company first had part of reactor

indicators.note: says the company abbreviation comes before the engineers

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: An engineering firm got hold of a part of a reactor first.
explanation.definitionFit: The central section of a nuclear reactor, holding the fuel, is called its core.

clue.text: Tending to excite expert on case

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: Something arouses an expert working on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a detective's investigation, but it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Provocative means deliberately arousing a strong reaction or excitement.

clue.text: Carol's ringers give succession of tinkling sounds first

definitions.note: the possessive here reads as carol is, so the clue says the carol equals what follows

indicators.note: says the tinkling sounds come before the ringers

parts.note: a jingle is a run of light ringing sounds
bells are things that ring

explanation.surface: A woman's bell-ringers produce tinkling sounds first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol's' looks like a woman's name in the possessive; it is the Christmas song plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Christmas song, the kind sung by carollers.

clue.text: Are dropping one outlet for reprint

indicators.note: the word Are lets fall the letter that means one

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item
an issue is a way out, an outlet for water

explanation.surface: A publisher's outlet stops a reprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes the A out of ARE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a fresh printing or release of something published before.

clue.text: Terminal's high cost

definitions.meaning: an electrical terminal connected to the ground
as in the phrase it costs the world, a huge price

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a ground connection in wiring and appears in the idiom of costing a fortune.

clue.text: Nevertheless short time afterwards produced idea

indicators.note: says the time letter is placed after the first piece

parts.note: though means however or nevertheless
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: After a short delay, someone came up with an idea anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought is an idea or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: This river goes in opposite directions from time to time

definitions.text: This river goes in opposite directions from time to time

parts.words: This river goes in opposite directions from time to time
parts.note: describes a river whose lower reaches flow inland and out again with the sea's daily rise and fall

explanation.definitionFit: A river affected by the sea's ebb and flow reverses direction with each change of water level.

clue.text: Look round street guide with individual in Rome area

indicators.note: the word for look goes around the other pieces

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
an A to Z is a British street map book
I as the Roman numeral one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A tourist checks a street map with someone in the Roman countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: An A–Z is the standard British book of street maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazio is the Italian region that contains Rome.

clue.text: Star lass leaving gambling city

indicators.note: the letters of lass depart from the city name

parts.note: Las Vegas in Nevada is famous for its casinos
taken as written, a girl

explanation.surface: A starlet walks out of Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters L, A, S, S come out of LAS VEGAS in order, leaving the star's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Animals rush back

indicators.note: the plant word is read from end to start

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant

explanation.surface: Animals hurry back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' looks like a verb meaning hurry; it is the marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of this word refers to several of the antlered animals.

clue.text: Book that's finally inconclusive

indicators.note: without its conclusion, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A book that turns out to have an open ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps.

clue.text: Onslaught a sailor reported

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is said to have been attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack, an onslaught.

clue.text: Not one increase could be genuine

indicators.note: the remaining letters may be rearranged into something else
says the letter for one is left out of increase

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: A pay rise without a single penny can hardly be genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' removes A from INCREASE, leaving INCRESE, which 'could be' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and genuine in feeling.

clue.text: Treasure potential riches with aspiration

indicators.note: the letters of riches could potentially form a different word

parts.note: H is the breathed sound, an aspirate

explanation.surface: Wealth has potential if pursued with ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition; in phonetics it is the breathy sound of H.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to cherish it, to value it dearly.

clue.text: In Laos I disrupted connection

indicators.note: the letters of In Laos I are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Communications were cut while I was in Laos.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a link or working connection between people or groups.

clue.text: Incomplete chirp that is quaint

indicators.note: the bird sound is left without its last letter

parts.note: a tweet is a bird's chirp

explanation.surface: A bird's half-finished chirp is rather charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sweet.

clue.text: Dental exam?

parts.note: a test of the mouth, which is what a dentist checks, but read as a spoken test rather than a written one

explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination is named for the mouth, the very thing a dentist inspects.

clue.text: Man, I'll say

indicators.note: signals that I'll is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: A man gives his word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is one example of an island.

clue.text: Greek character getting in the way of soot

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes inside the abbreviation for way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man finds soot blocking his path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is a flake of soot or dirty particles.

clue.text: Arguing about mere squalor developing

indicators.note: the letters of mere squalor are developing into a new form

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a bit of growing filth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quarrelsome is inclined to argue.

clue.text: Wicked French town had heart ripped out

indicators.note: the central letter of the French word is removed

parts.note: ville is the French word for town

explanation.surface: Something wicked tore the centre out of a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile means wicked or morally despicable.

clue.text: Even so you need to be present for whole of athletics meeting

definitions.text: you need to be present for whole of athletics meeting
definitions.meaning: taken literally, you must attend every contest of the track meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning in any case also literally describes attending every race and field contest.
